scenes.heading: Reading test strategies
scenes.sub: Finish every passage and prove every answer
scenes.say: Thirty questions, thirty minutes, and a pile of passages. How do you finish on time and still get the answers right? You need a plan.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A detective points to clues before naming anyone
scenes.science: You point to words in the text before choosing an answer
scenes.breaks: a detective can search for days; you have about one minute per question, so you must move on.
scenes.say: Be a detective, not a fortune-teller. A detective points to a clue before naming a suspect. You point to the words in the passage before choosing an answer. But unlike a detective, you can't take days. You have about a minute per question.

scenes.heading: Six question shapes
scenes.say: Most reading questions fit six shapes. Fact-finding, main idea and purpose, inference, vocabulary in context, tone and technique, and structure. Naming the shape tells you where to look.

scenes.heading: Read, Predict, Eliminate, Prove
steps: Find the place in the text
Predict the answer in your words
Prove it with words from the text
scenes.say: Here's the method for every question. Read the stem. Find the place in the text. Predict the answer in your own words before looking at the options. Eliminate the wrong ones. Then prove your choice with words from the passage.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Why have the library's seed drawers never been empty?
lines: Predict: more come back than go out
scenes.say: In our library passage, why are the seed drawers never empty? It's fact-finding, so the answer is in the text. The last sentence says returned seeds outnumber borrowed ones. Predict: more come back than go out. That's option B.

scenes.heading: Spot the trap

left.title: Right answer
points: Backed by words you can point to
Says no more than the text

right.title: Distractor
points: True, but answers a different question

scenes.say: A right answer matches the exact question and you can point to its evidence. Distractors are often true details that don't answer the question, or they use extreme words like always, never or proved.

points: Read stems first, then the passage
Predict before you look at options
scenes.say: Quick recap. Allow about a minute per question. Read the stems, then the passage. Predict, eliminate and prove. Skip slow questions, come back later, and leave nothing blank. Now try the practice questions!
